mainTopic: פסי ביראות and which תנאים the משנה fits; then דיומדין and רבי ירמיה בן אלעזר's teaching that אדם הראשון had two faces
overview: This amud finishes the משנה about פסי ביראות, the boards placed around a well so that festival pilgrims can water their animals on שבת. The תנא קמא lets the enclosure be any size, as long as more boards are added, while רבי יהודה limits it to בית סאתים. The חכמים answer that this limit applies only to a גינה or קרפף. The גמרא then checks whether the משנה can fit the views of חנניא, רבי עקיבא and רבי יהודה בן בבא, and each time it shows that it can. Next it explains the word דיומדין as 'two posts' (דיו עמודין) from רבי ירמיה בן אלעזר. This leads to a list of his other teachings, beginning with his statement that אדם הראשון was created with two faces. רב and שמואל argue whether the צלע used to build חוה was a face or a tail. The גמרא tests both views against several פסוקים. The discussion of 'ויבן' continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The enclosure may be made as big as you like
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא of the משנה rules that the boards may be pushed out to any distance from the well, as long as extra boards are added.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is permitted to move the boards out any distance, as long as he adds more boards.
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes the תנא קמא's ruling that began on the previous amud: the boards around the well can be moved outward without limit. The only condition is that more upright boards are added in the gaps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Moving the boards outward makes the gaps between the corner posts wider. Adding more upright boards keeps those gaps small enough that the enclosure still counts as a מחיצה. So there is no limit on size, only a requirement about how the enclosure is built.

keyTerms.meaning: to move farther away (here, moving the boards out from the well)
upright boards used to enclose an area around a well

phrases.english: to distance [the boards] by any amount,
phrases.notes: Continues 'it is permitted' from the end of the previous amud.

phrases.english: provided that he increases the boards.
phrases.notes: More boards keep the gaps between them from getting too wide.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the תנא קמא's ruling that began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The enclosure of פסי ביראות may be any size, as long as enough boards are added.

steps.title: רבי יהודה limits the size to בית סאתים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה disagrees and says the enclosure may only be as large as בית סאתים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: only up to an area of בית סאתים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה gives a different opinion. He holds that the enclosed area around the well may not be bigger than בית סאתים (5,000 square אמות).
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית סאתים is a familiar measurement in הלכות שבת. It is the largest area that is not used for living, like a קרפף, which one may still carry in. רבי יהודה applies that same limit to the area around the well.

keyTerms.meaning: an area of 5,000 square אמות, roughly 50×100

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
up to [an area of] two beit se'a.
phrases.notes: 5,000 square cubits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא by placing a size limit on the enclosure.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The enclosure around a well may be no larger than בית סאתים.

steps.title: The חכמים say the בית סאתים limit applies only to a garden or storage yard
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer רבי יהודה. The בית סאתים limit was said only about a גינה or קרפף. A pen, stable, backyard or courtyard can be huge, and so can the area around the well.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: the בית סאתים limit was only said about a garden or a storage enclosure. But a pen, a stable, a backyard or a courtyard is permitted even at five בית כור, even at ten בית כור. And it is permitted to move the boards out any distance, as long as he adds more boards.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back on רבי יהודה. They say the source of the בית סאתים limit does not apply here, and then repeat the תנא קמא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים explain that בית סאתים is a limit for places that people do not use all the time, like a גינה or a קרפף. Places that serve a house or animals, like a דיר, סהר, מוקצה or חצר, have no size limit, even at ten בית כור. The area around a well serves animals, so it also has no limit. That is why the משנה ends by repeating the rule that the boards may be moved out any distance.

keyTerms.meaning: an enclosed area used for storage, not for living
areas measured in kor; one בית כור equals 30 בית סאה

steps.confusionAlert: Here מוקצה means a backyard. It does NOT mean the familiar מוקצה, objects that may not be moved on שבת.
steps.whatToRemember: According to the חכמים, the בית סאתים limit applies only to areas like a גינה or קרפף. Places used for animals or for the house, including the area around a well, can be any size.

phrases.english: They said to him:
They did not say [the limit of] two beit se'a
except for a garden or a storage enclosure,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אִם הָיָה דִּיר אוֹ סַהַר
phrases.english: but if it was a pen or a stable
or a backyard or a courtyard —
even an area of five beit kor,
even an area of ten beit kor, it is permitted.
And it is permitted to distance [the boards] any amount,
phrases.notes: The משנה itself repeats the תנא קמא's rule here.

phrases.english: provided that he increases the boards.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: לֹא אָמְרוּ בֵּית סָאתַיִם אֶלָּא לְגִנָּה וּלְקַרְפֵּף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי יהודה's limit by showing it belongs only to a different kind of area, and goes back to the תנא קמא's rule.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects applying the בית סאתים limit to the area around the well.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יהודה took a limit that applies only to a גינה or קרפף and applied it to places that serve animals or a house.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Areas used for animals or for the house have no size limit, so the boards may be moved out any distance.

steps.title: Does our משנה disagree with חנניא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the משנה, which allows boards around a well, goes against חנניא. In a ברייתא, חנניא says a בור may get ropes but not boards.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say our משנה is not like חנניא. For a ברייתא teaches: one may make boards for a cistern and ropes for a caravan. חנניא says: ropes for a cistern, but not boards.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and suggests that our משנה goes against the opinion of חנניא. It brings a ברייתא to show this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא of the ברייתא allows פסין around a בור. חנניא allows only ropes there, not boards. Our משנה clearly allows פסין around a well, so it seems to follow the תנא קמא of the ברייתא and to disagree with חנניא.

keyTerms.meaning: shall we say? (the גמרא proposes something to check)
a pit that holds collected rainwater

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Let us say our Mishnah is not in accordance with Chananya,
as it was taught [in a Baraita]:
One may make boards for a cistern
and ropes for a caravan.
And Chananya says:
ropes for a cistern,
but not boards.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא by checking which תנא the משנה's rule about פסין fits with.
steps.kashyaTarget: Whether the משנה can follow חנניא's opinion.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה allows פסין around a water source, but חנניא forbids פסין around a בור. So the משנה seems to disagree with him.

steps.title: A cistern is different from a well
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה can follow חנניא too. חנניא spoke about a בור, which is different from a באר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if you say [the משנה follows] חנניא: a cistern is one thing and a well is another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the idea that the משנה disagrees with חנניא. It explains that a בור and a באר are not the same case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בור holds collected rainwater that will eventually run out, so permanent boards would end up useless. That is why חנניא forbids them. A באר is a spring that keeps flowing, so boards around it stay useful, and חנניא could agree to the משנה's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: a well of flowing spring water

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה can follow חנניא too. חנניא's ruling against boards was said only about a בור of collected rainwater, not about a flowing באר.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up בור and באר. A בור is a pit of collected rainwater. A באר is a natural spring.

phrases.english: Even if you say [it follows] Chananya,
a cistern is separate,
phrases.notes: A cistern holds collected water, which can run out.

phrases.english: and a well is separate.
phrases.notes: A well has spring water that keeps flowing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the suggestion that the משנה disagrees with חנניא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because חנניא forbids פסין around a בור, we thought he would forbid them around every water source, which would contradict the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: חנניא forbids פסין only around a בור, whose water runs out. A באר keeps flowing, so the משנה can follow him.

steps.title: Second version: חנניא makes no difference between a cistern and a well
steps.stepSummary: In a second version of the earlier discussion, the גמרא reasons from what חנניא did not say. If he had held that a באר is different, he would have said so. So for him both a בור and a באר get only ropes, not boards. That would go against our משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it this way: The ברייתא does not say 'חנניא says: one makes ropes for a cistern and boards for a well.' This shows that for חנניא there is no difference between a cistern and a well. Ropes, yes. Boards, no. So should we say our משנה does not follow חנניא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version (איכא דאמרי) of the challenge from חנניא. Here it learns from his silence that he gives no boards even to a באר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version (Step 5), the גמרא escaped by saying חנניא spoke only about a בור. This version blocks that escape. If חנניא held a באר is different, the ברייתא should have quoted him saying so. Since it did not, he seems to treat both the same, and that clashes with our משנה, which allows boards around wells.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say: a second version of the same discussion
By inference; we can conclude from this
Ropes (strung around as a makeshift enclosure)
Upright boards placed around a well

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question. It is a second version of the challenge in Steps 4–5. The only difference is the reasoning: here the גמרא learns from what חנניא left out.

phrases.english: Some say:
phrases.notes: Here comes another way of telling the passage we just learned.

phrases.english: From the fact that it does not teach:
'Chananya says: one makes ropes for a cistern
and boards for a well,'
this implies that according to Chananya

phrases.aramaic: לָא שְׁנָא בּוֹר וְלָא שְׁנָא בְּאֵר —
phrases.english: there is no difference between a cistern and a well:
ropes, yes; boards, no.
Shall we say our Mishnah is not like Chananya?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restates the חנניא challenge in a version that blocks the distinction made in Step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: Our משנה, which allows boards (פסין) around wells.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since the ברייתא is silent, חנניא must give only ropes to both a בור and a באר. That contradicts the משנה, which gives boards to a באר.

steps.title: חנניא was only answering what the תנא קמא said
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that חנניא could agree that a באר gets boards. He did not mention it because he was only replying to the תנא קמא, who spoke only about a בור.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say the משנה follows חנניא. He was only responding to what the תנא קמא said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the inference from silence. חנניא simply stayed on the topic the תנא קמא raised.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on 'he should have mentioned a באר.' But the תנא קמא only discussed a בור, so חנניא had no reason to bring up a באר. His silence proves nothing, and the משנה can still follow him.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you say: the משנה can still fit this view
The first, unnamed opinion in a teaching
He was replying to him (responding on his terms)

steps.whatToRemember: In both versions, the משנה can follow חנניא. Either he spoke only about a בור, or he was only answering the תנא קמא.

phrases.english: Even if you say it follows Chananya,
to what the first Tanna said
he was replying to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Context of the statement: the silence is explained by the scope of the discussion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since חנניא did not mention a באר, he must hold that it too gets only ropes.
steps.terutzMaskana: חנניא only addressed the בור that the תנא קמא raised. He may well allow boards for a באר.

steps.title: Does the משנה go against רבי עקיבא? His ruling on cisterns and wells
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that our משנה goes against רבי עקיבא. It quotes his ruling: a public well, a public cistern, and a private well all get boards. Only a private cistern needs a full ten-טפחים wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say our משנה does not follow רבי עקיבא? We learned in a משנה: A public well, a public cistern, and a private well all get boards. But a private cistern needs a wall ten טפחים high. These are the words of רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new challenge and brings the source it needs: רבי עקיבא's ruling. This sets up the contrast with our משנה in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key point is that רבי עקיבא allows boards for a public בור (cistern), not only for wells. He requires a real wall only for a private cistern. The next step will show why this seems to clash with our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
A partition ten handbreadths high (a full, proper wall)

steps.confusionAlert: Know the two words apart. A בור is a cistern that collects rainwater. A באר is a well fed by a spring. רבי עקיבא gives boards to a public בור as well.

phrases.english: Shall we say our Mishnah is not like Rabbi Akiva?
For we learned:
Whether a public well or a public cistern
or a private well, one makes boards for them.
But a private cistern:

phrases.aramaic: עוֹשִׂין לוֹ מְחִיצָה גָּבוֹהַּ עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים,
phrases.english: one makes for it a partition ten handbreadths high;
these are the words of Rabbi Akiva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After resolving חנניא, the גמרא tests the משנה against another תנא, רבי עקיבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: Our משנה's rule of boards for wells.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי עקיבא allows boards for a public cistern. Step 9 will show that our משנה seems to limit boards to wells.

steps.title: Our משנה says boards are for wells only, not cisterns
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes the contrast. Our משנה says boards are 'for wells.' That implies wells yes, cisterns no, which goes against רבי עקיבא's allowance for a public cistern.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here our משנה says: 'for wells.' For wells, yes. For cisterns, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge by drawing an inference from the wording of our משנה. The answer will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'לביראות' (for wells) suggests that only wells get boards. Cisterns, even public ones, would not. רבי עקיבא allowed boards for a public בור, so our משנה seems to disagree with him.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the גמרא builds a contradiction from the exact wording of a משנה. A single word ('wells') is read as excluding cisterns.

phrases.english: Whereas here it teaches: 'for wells.'
For wells, yes; for cisterns, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge from Step 8 by contrasting it with the wording of our משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Our משנה implies that cisterns get no boards. רבי עקיבא gives boards to a public cistern, so the two seem to contradict.

steps.title: The משנה can follow רבי עקיבא after all
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה can match רבי עקיבא. It mentions only wells because their rule is simple, and it leaves out cisterns because their rule depends on who owns them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if you say the משנה follows רבי עקיבא, there is no problem. The משנה teaches the case of a well of spring water, because its rule is clear-cut: it does not matter whether it is public or private. It does not teach the case of a cistern of collected rainwater, because its rule is not clear-cut.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends our משנה against the challenge from רבי עקיבא. It explains why the משנה mentions only wells and not cisterns.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי עקיבא, every באר gets boards, public or private. A בור gets boards only when it is public. Since the משנה could not state one simple rule for a בור, it left the בור out. Leaving it out does not mean that a public בור is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you say: the משנה can fit this opinion too
A well of fresh spring water, fed from underground
It is clear-cut for him: one rule with no exceptions

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה's silence about a בור is not a ruling against it. The משנה simply avoided a case that would need splitting into public and private.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common way the גמרא reads a משנה. Sometimes a משנה teaches only the cases with a clean, unconditional rule.

phrases.english: Even if you say it follows Rabbi Akiva,
a well of spring water,
which is clear-cut for him,
no difference whether it belongs to the public
and no difference whether it belongs to an individual: this he teaches.
phrases.notes: Every well gets boards, so the משנה can state it without conditions.

phrases.english: A cistern of collected water,
which is not clear-cut for him: this he does not teach.
phrases.notes: A public cistern gets boards, but a private one does not, so there is no single rule.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of steps 8–9, which said the משנה excludes cisterns and so goes against רבי עקיבא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting why the משנה is silent: it left the case out because the rule has conditions, not because the case is excluded.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Saying 'for wells' implies that no cistern gets boards, which would contradict רבי עקיבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה lists only the case with an unconditional rule (wells). It leaves cisterns unaddressed, so it fits רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: Does the משנה contradict רבי יהודה בן בבא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes that our משנה goes against רבי יהודה בן בבא. He allows boards only for a public well, while our משנה's plural 'wells' seems to include private wells too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say our משנה does not follow רבי יהודה בן בבא. We learned in a משנה: רבי יהודה בן בבא says, boards may be set up only for a public well. But here the משנה says 'for wells,' which implies it makes no difference whether public or private.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge from a different תנא. It sets רבי יהודה בן בבא's narrow rule against the משנה's broad wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה בן בבא limits boards to a public באר only. Our משנה uses the plural 'ביראות' with no limits, which sounds like every well, private ones included. If that reading is right, the משנה cannot match his view.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say: introduces a suggested conclusion
As we learned in a משנה
Upright boards placed around a well so one may draw water on שבת

phrases.english: Shall we say that our Mishnah
is not in line with Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava?

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בָּבָא אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: For we learned: Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava says:
One may not set up boards
except for a public well alone.
Whereas here it teaches 'for wells,'
phrases.notes: The question comes from the word being plural: 'wells,' not 'a well.'

phrases.english: implying no difference whether public
and no difference whether private!

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בָּבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After resolving רבי עקיבא, the גמרא tests the משנה against another תנא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The broad wording of our משנה: 'for wells.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The plural 'wells' with no limits implies private wells are included. רבי יהודה בן בבא forbids boards for private wells.

steps.title: 'Wells' means the ordinary public wells
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'wells' in the משנה means the wells of the world, the common wells everyone uses. So the משנה can match רבי יהודה בן בבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if you say the משנה follows רבי יהודה בן בבא, there is no problem. What does 'wells' mean? The wells of the world, the ones everyone uses, which are public wells.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the משנה by explaining the word 'wells' more narrowly. That reading lets the משנה fit רבי יהודה בן בבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plural does not have to mean 'every kind of well.' 'בֵּירָאוֹת דְּעָלְמָא' means the wells used by the general public. That limits the משנה to public wells, which is exactly רבי יהודה בן בבא's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Of the world: belonging to or used by everyone

steps.whatToRemember: Our משנה about boards for wells can fit רבי עקיבא, because it only mentions the case with a clear-cut rule. It can also fit רבי יהודה בן בבא, because 'wells' means the public wells everyone uses.

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בָּבָא,
phrases.english: Even if you say it follows Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava,
what is meant by 'wells'?
Wells of the world.
phrases.notes: These are the common wells used by everyone, meaning public wells.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בָּבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining a term: 'wells' is read narrowly.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Wells' in the plural includes both public and private wells.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Wells' means the public wells everyone uses, matching רבי יהודה בן בבא.

steps.title: What does the word דיומדין mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to a new topic: explaining the unusual word דיומדין used in the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are דיומדין?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new section that explains a word in the משנה. This question sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה calls the corner pieces of the enclosure around a well דיומדין, an unusual word. Before discussing their rules, the גמרא needs to know exactly what they are.

keyTerms.meaning: A word in the משנה for the corner pieces of the boards around a well

phrases.english: What are deyomadin?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: it moves from which תנא the משנה follows to the meaning of a word in it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word דיומדין in the משנה.

steps.title: דיומדין means two posts
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה בן אלעזר explains that דיומדין is a compound word, 'דיו עמודין,' meaning two posts joined to form one corner piece.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה בן אלעזר said: דיומדין means 'two posts.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה בן אלעזר answers the question by breaking the word into two parts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'דיו' means two, and 'עמודין' means posts. So each corner piece around the well is made of two boards joined at an angle, one facing each direction.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya ben Elazar said:
Two posts.
phrases.notes: The two posts are joined to make one corner piece.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר: דְּיוֹ עַמּוּדִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: דיומדין is a compound of 'דיו' (two) and 'עמודין' (posts): two posts forming one corner piece.

steps.title: A memory aid for a list of teachings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a string of code words. Each word reminds the learner of an upcoming teaching by רבי ירמיה בן אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two, to one who was ostracized, praise, nourishment, ruin, attribute, three: these are memory signs.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא lists short code words that will help you remember the coming teachings of רבי ירמיה בן אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just saw רבי ירמיה בן אלעזר explain דיומדין with the word דיו. Because of that, the גמרא now collects more of his statements. Each code word is a hint for one statement. The first one, דיו, is his teaching about two faces in Step 18, which comes right after a short side point from עולא on another דיו word.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid; code words that help remember a series of teachings
Two (from Greek). It is the link word for this whole section

steps.confusionAlert: These words are not a sentence and have no meaning together. Each word is only a reminder of a separate teaching.

phrases.english: Two, to one who was ostracized, praise, nourishment,
phrases.notes: Each word hints at a separate teaching

phrases.english: ruin, attribute, three: these are memory signs.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּיוֹ לִמְנוּדֶּה שֶׁבַח זוֹנִית נִתְקַלְקֵל בְּמִידָּה שְׁלֹשָׁה סִימָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on Step 14's use of דיו and opens a collection of רבי ירמיה בן אלעזר's teachings
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A memory aid for a list of teachings by רבי ירמיה בן אלעזר

steps.title: What is a דיופרא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה where רבי יהודה exempts poor-quality figs from tithing, except for דיופרא. Then it asks what דיופרא means.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: רבי יהודה says, all poor-quality figs are exempt, except for the דיופרא. What is a דיופרא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another word that contains דיו and asks what it means. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה says inferior figs bought from an עם הארץ do not need to be tithed as דמאי. The seller surely already tithed them, since the loss is so small. He makes one exception, דיופרא, and the גמרא wants to know what that word refers to.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned there, in a משנה in another place
A special tree whose name means 'two fruits'

phrases.english: We learned there: Rabbi Yehuda says:
All inferior figs are exempt,
phrases.notes: Exempt from tithing as דמאי

phrases.english: except for the deyufra.
What is deyufra?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another word containing דיו, brought in alongside רבי ירמיה בן אלעזר's teachings
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word דיופרא

steps.title: עולא: a tree that fruits twice a year
steps.stepSummary: עולא explains that דיופרא is a tree that gives two harvests each year.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: It is a tree that produces two crops of fruit a year.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers the question. דיופרא means 'two fruits,' a tree that bears fruit twice a year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word splits into דיו ('two') and פרא ('fruit'). This works just like דיומדין, 'two posts.' The fruit of such a tree is valuable, so it is not treated like ordinary inferior figs.

phrases.english: Ulla said:
A tree that produces two crops of fruit a year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 16
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: דיופרא = דיו פירות, a tree that gives two harvests a year

steps.title: אדם הראשון was created with two faces
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה בן אלעזר teaches that אדם הראשון was first created with two faces. He proves it from the verse 'אחור וקדם צרתני.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה בן אלעזר said: אדם הראשון had two faces, as it says, 'You formed me behind and before.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first teaching from the memory list, the word דיו. רבי ירמיה בן אלעזר says אדם was created with two faces, one in front and one in back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse in תהלים says 'behind and before You formed me.' He reads it literally: אדם was formed with a face on both sides. One explanation is that one face was male and the other female.

keyTerms.meaning: A face; a full facial form
'Behind and before You formed me' (תהלים קלט:ה)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya ben Elazar said:
Two faces
the first man had,
as it is stated: "Behind and before You formed me."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר: דְּיוֹ פַּרְצוּף פָּנִים הָיָה לוֹ לְאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first teaching cued by the memory word דיו
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אדם הראשון was created with two faces, based on 'אחור וקדם צרתני'

steps.title: רב and שמואל argue about the צלע
steps.stepSummary: On the verse 'ויבן ה׳ אלקים את הצלע,' רב and שמואל disagree. One says the צלע was a face, and the other says it was a tail.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written: 'And the Lord God built the צלע...' רב and שמואל disagree: one says it was a face, and one says it was a tail.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a disagreement about what part of אדם was used to build חוה. One view says a whole face, and the other says a tail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'face' opinion fits רבי ירמיה בן אלעזר's two-faces teaching: חוה was built from the second face. The 'tail' opinion says אדם had only one face plus a tail, and חוה was built from that tail. This difference sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Usually translated 'rib'; here debated as a face or a tail
One said (the גמרא does not tell us who said which)

steps.confusionAlert: The צלע here is not taken as a simple 'rib.' Both opinions read it as something bigger, either a face or a tail.

phrases.aramaic: כְּתִיב: ״וַיִּבֶן ה׳ אֱלֹהִים אֶת הַצֵּלָע וְגוֹ׳״,
phrases.english: It is written: "And the Lord God built the tzela, etc."
Rav and Shmuel:
one said it was a face,
and one said it was a tail.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל: חַד אָמַר פַּרְצוּף, וְחַד אָמַר זָנָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a מחלוקת related to the two-faces teaching
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The צלע was either a face (agreeing with two faces) or a tail

steps.title: How does the tail view explain 'behind and before'?
steps.stepSummary: The face view fits the verse 'אחור וקדם צרתני' well. The גמרא challenges the tail view: what does that verse mean for it?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for the one who says 'face': that is why it is written 'You formed me behind and before.' But for the one who says 'tail,' what does 'You formed me behind and before' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes on the 'tail' opinion. The verse seems to support two faces, so how does the tail opinion read it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בשלמא formula means: we understand one side, but the other side is hard. 'Behind and before' matches a face in front and a face in back. If אדם had only a tail, the verse needs another explanation, and the גמרא asks what it is.

keyTerms.meaning: It is understandable (according to one view)
According to the one who says

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who says 'face':
that is why it is written: "Behind and before You formed me."
But according to the one who says 'tail':
what is "Behind and before You formed me"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the 'tail' side of the מחלוקת in Step 19
steps.kashyaTarget: The opinion that the צלע was a tail
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse 'אחור וקדם צרתני' points to two faces. The tail view seems to have no explanation for it.

steps.title: רבי אמי's reading answers the tail view
steps.stepSummary: The tail view explains 'אחור וקדם צרתני' as רבי אמי does: אדם was last in creation and first in punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse follows רבי אמי, who said: 'Behind' means אדם came last in the work of creation, and 'before' means he came first for punishment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 20. The one who says the צלע was a tail does not read 'אחור וקדם' as two faces. He reads it the way רבי אמי does, about the order of events.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The face view read 'אחור וקדם' physically, as a front face and a back face. The tail view reads it as being about time. אדם was 'behind' because he was created last, and 'before' because he was punished first. Read this way, the verse no longer proves two faces, so the tail view survives.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא whose teaching explains the verse

phrases.english: Like Rabbi Ami,
for Rabbi Ami said:
'Behind' means last in the work of creation,
and 'before' means first for punishment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 20
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'אחור וקדם' must mean two physical faces
steps.terutzMaskana: 'אחור וקדם' can mean last in creation and first in punishment

steps.title: What does 'first for punishment' mean?
steps.stepSummary: Being last in creation is clear. But 'first for punishment' does not fit the curses, because the נחש and חוה were cursed before אדם.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that אדם was 'behind', meaning last in creation, since he was not created until ערב שבת. But what does 'before for punishment' mean? If you say it refers to the curse, that does not work. First the נחש was cursed, then חוה, and only at the end אדם!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the first half of רבי אמי's reading. It then questions the second half. It also rejects the most obvious explanation, the curses after the sin with the עץ הדעת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אדם being last in creation is easy to see, because he was made on the sixth day. 'First in punishment' is harder. The order of the curses in the פסוקים is נחש, then חוה, then אדם. So אדם was actually cursed last, not first.

phrases.english: Granted, 'behind' meaning last in the work of creation
makes sense, since he was not created until Shabbat eve,
but 'before, for punishment', what is this?
If you say it is because of the curse,
but first the snake was cursed,
afterward Eve was cursed,
and only at the end was Adam cursed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second half of רבי אמי's reading
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the order of the curses, אדם was last, not first

steps.title: First for punishment means the מבול
steps.stepSummary: 'First for punishment' refers to the מבול, where the פסוק lists אדם first among those destroyed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it refers to the Flood. The פסוק says: 'He wiped out every living thing on the face of the earth, from man to animal...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 22. 'First for punishment' does not mean the curses. It means the מבול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק about the מבול, the list of who was destroyed begins with אדם ('מאדם') and then goes on to the animals. That makes man first in this punishment. So רבי אמי's reading holds, and the tail view still has an explanation of 'אחור וקדם'.
steps.whatToRemember: According to the tail view, 'אחור וקדם צרתני' means אדם was last in creation and first in punishment, at the מבול.

phrases.english: Rather, it refers to the Flood, as it is written:
'And He wiped out every living thing
that was on the face of the ground,
from man to animal, etc.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 22
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'First for punishment' refers to the curses after the sin
steps.terutzMaskana: It refers to the מבול, where man is listed first

steps.title: Why does 'וייצר' have two יודין?
steps.stepSummary: The face view explains the double יוד in 'וייצר' as two formations. The tail view needs to explain it.
steps.simpleTranslation: For the one who says the צלע was a face, it makes sense that 'וייצר' is written with two יודין. But for the one who says it was a tail, what does 'וייצר' teach?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge against the tail view, this time from the spelling of a word. It sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'וייצר' (He formed) is spelled with an extra יוד. The face view says this hints at two formations: one creature with two faces, later made into אדם and חוה. The tail view needs a different reason for the double יוד.

keyTerms.meaning: And He formed, spelled with two יודין

steps.confusionAlert: This is a new challenge, separate from 'אחור וקדם'. Now the question is about spelling: why two יודין instead of one.

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who says it was a face,
that is why 'vayyitzer' is written with two yuds.
But according to the one who says it was a tail,
what does 'vayyitzer' teach?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first challenge is resolved, a second challenge to the tail view begins
steps.kashyaTarget: The tail view of the צלע
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The double יוד hints at two formations, which fits only the face view

steps.title: The double letter teaches that a person is pulled two ways
steps.stepSummary: The tail view explains the two יודין in 'וייצר' with רבי שמעון בן פזי: a person is caught between his יצר and his יוצר.
steps.simpleTranslation: It follows רבי שמעון בן פזי, who said: Woe to me from my inclination, and woe to me from my Maker.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 24. The tail view says the two יודין do not mean two formations. They point to the two forces a person must face.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'וייצר' sounds like both יצר (inclination) and יוצר (Maker). If a person follows his Maker, his inclination gives him trouble. If he follows his inclination, he must answer to his Maker. So the extra letter is about human struggle, not about two bodies.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And He formed', the word spelled with two יודין

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the tail view denies that there are two יודין. It agrees about the letters and only reads them differently: as two pulls inside a person, not two creations.

phrases.english: In line with Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi,
for Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi said:
Woe to me from my inclination,
phrases.notes: If I obey my Maker, my inclination troubles me.

phrases.english: woe to me from my Maker.
phrases.notes: If I obey my inclination, I must answer to my Maker.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 24 about the double יוד.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative reading of the verse: the double letter is a moral lesson, not two physical formations.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two יודין show that אדם was formed twice, as two faces, which supports only the face view.
steps.terutzMaskana: The two יודין hint at יצר and יוצר, the two forces a person stands between. This fits the tail view.

steps.title: How does the tail view read 'Male and female He created them'?
steps.stepSummary: The face view easily explains 'זכר ונקבה בראם' as two faces from the start. The גמרא asks what the verse means for the tail view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, for the one who says 'face', that is why it is written 'Male and female He created them.' But for the one who says 'tail', what does 'Male and female He created them' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new verse that seems to favor the face view and challenges the tail view with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'זכר ונקבה בראם' sounds as if male and female were created together at the very start. That matches the face view, where אדם was made with two faces. The tail view says only one person was made at first, so it must explain the verse.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, it makes sense (opens a contrast challenge)
Face, the view that אדם had two faces
Tail, the view that חוה was made from a tail-like part

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who says 'face',
that is why it is written 'Male and female He created them.'
But according to the one who says 'tail',
what does 'Male and female He created them' mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same 'granted for the face view, but the tail view?' pattern with a new verse.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The plural 'them' points to male and female existing from the start, which fits two faces but not a single original body.

steps.title: Two were planned, but only one was created
steps.stepSummary: The tail view explains the verse with רבי אבהו: the plural 'them' describes the original plan, but in the end only one was created.
steps.simpleTranslation: It follows רבי אבהו. רבי אבהו pointed out a contradiction: it is written 'Male and female He created them,' and it is written 'In the image of God He created him.' At first the thought was to create two, and in the end only one was created.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge of step 26 by quoting רבי אבהו, who saw two verses that seem to clash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One verse says 'them' (plural) and another says 'him' (singular). רבי אבהו settles this: the plural describes what was first planned, two people, and the singular describes what was actually made, one person. So 'זכר ונקבה בראם' does not prove two faces, and the tail view is safe.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised a contradiction between two sources
It arose in thought, it was planned

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read רבי אבהו as saying two people were actually made. The 'two' was only a plan. In fact only one was created, and חוה was taken from him later.

phrases.english: It comes to teach as Rabbi Abahu taught.
For Rabbi Abahu raised a contradiction:
It is written 'Male and female He created them,'
phrases.notes: Notice 'them' here is plural.

phrases.english: and it is written '(for) in the image of God He created him.'
phrases.notes: But here 'him' is singular.

phrases.english: At first it arose in thought to create two,
and in the end only one was created.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reconciling two verses: one describes the plan, the other describes what actually happened.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Male and female He created them' means two beings or faces were actually made at the start.
steps.terutzMaskana: The plural describes only the original plan. In fact one person was created, which fits the tail view.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common method: when two verses seem to clash, one can describe the plan and the other the final result.

steps.title: How does the tail view read 'He closed up the flesh in its place'?
steps.stepSummary: The face view easily explains 'ויסגור בשר תחתנה'. The גמרא asks how the tail view explains it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, for the one who says 'face', that is why it is written 'And He closed up the flesh in its place.' But for the one who says 'tail', what does 'And He closed up the flesh in its place' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises another verse-based challenge against the tail view. It is setting up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a whole face-side was removed from אדם, a large opening was left, so the flesh had to be closed up. If only a small tail was taken, it is less clear why the verse stresses closing flesh. The tail view must explain the verse.

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who says 'face',
that is why it is written 'And He closed up the flesh in its place,'
but according to the one who says 'tail',
what does 'And He closed up the flesh in its place' mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the previous challenge is answered, the גמרא brings a new verse in the same pattern.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Closing up flesh suggests a large opening, like one left by removing a whole face-side, not a small tail.

steps.title: The tail view explains 'closing the flesh' as closing the cut
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד (or רבי ירמיה, or רב נחמן בר יצחק) answers for the tail view. The verse about closing the flesh is needed only for the place where the cut was made.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד said (some say it was רבי ירמיה, and some say רב נחמן בר יצחק): The verse was needed only for the place of the cut.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 28. According to the tail view, the verse 'and He closed up the flesh' describes sealing the spot where the tail was cut off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The face view read 'ויסגור בשר תחתנה' as closing up a big open side after a whole face was removed. The tail view says that taking even a small tail still leaves a cut. The verse teaches that הקדוש ברוך הוא sealed that cut, so the verse makes sense for this view too.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (introduces another possible author of the same statement)

steps.confusionAlert: The three names do not give three different answers. The גמרא is unsure who said this one answer, so it lists all three possibilities.

phrases.english: Rav Zevid said,
and some say it was Rabbi Yirmeya,
and some say it was Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak:
It was needed only for the place of the cut.
phrases.notes: The 'closing of flesh' refers to sealing the spot where the tail was removed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 28 on behalf of the tail view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the verse to a smaller application
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'ויסגור בשר תחתנה' seems to describe closing a large opening, which fits only the face view.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse describes closing the small cut left after the tail was removed, so it fits the tail view too.

steps.title: The word 'built' fits the tail view, but what does it mean for the face view?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now challenges the face view. 'ויבן' (He built) makes sense if חוה was built up from a tail. If she was already a complete face, what was left to build?
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for the one who says 'tail': that is why it is written 'And He built.' But for the one who says 'face', what does 'And He built' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא flips the direction of the questions. It now asks the face view to explain a verse that fits the tail view better.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If חוה came from a small tail, הקדוש ברוך הוא really had to 'build' a whole person from it, so 'ויבן' fits perfectly. If she was already a full second face or side, she just needed to be separated. Then the word 'built' seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well (granted) for... (sets up a contrast)
That is why it is written

phrases.english: It works well for the one who says a tail,
that is why it is written: 'And He built,'
phrases.notes: Building a whole woman from a small tail is real 'building'.

phrases.english: but for the one who says a face —
what does 'And He built' mean?
phrases.notes: She was already complete, so what needed building?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר זָנָב, הַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב: ״וַיִּבֶן״, אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר פַּרְצוּף — מַאי ״וַיִּבֶן״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Up to now, the face view's verses challenged the tail view. Now a verse that suits the tail view challenges the face view.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Built' implies making something new. A complete face needed no building, so the face view seems to make the word pointless.

steps.title: 'Built' means הקדוש ברוך הוא braided חוה's hair
steps.stepSummary: The face view explains 'ויבן' using רבי שמעון בן מנסיא. הקדוש ברוך הוא braided חוה's hair and brought her to אדם. In the coastal towns, braiding is called 'building'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It follows רבי שמעון בן מנסיא, who taught on the verse 'And the Lord God built the צלע': This teaches that הקדוש ברוך הוא braided חוה's hair and brought her to אדם הראשון. In the coastal cities, braiding is called 'building'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for the face view. The word 'built' does not refer to making her body. It refers to braiding her hair, like adorning a bride before bringing her to אדם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The face view now has a job for the word 'ויבן'. It describes a different action, not the forming of her body. As proof, the גמרא points to how people speak: in the coastal towns, the word for 'building' is used for braiding hair.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the teaching of רבי...

steps.whyThisMatters: This teaching shows הקדוש ברוך הוא acting like a caring host at a wedding by preparing the bride. Other places in ש״ס use it to show the importance of honoring and beautifying a bride.

phrases.english: It follows the teaching of Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya.
For Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya expounded:
'And the Lord God built the tzela' —

phrases.aramaic: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁקִּילְּעָהּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְחַוָּה
phrases.english: this teaches that the Holy One, Blessed be He, braided Eve's hair
and brought her to Adam, the first man,
for in the coastal cities
they call braiding 'building'.
phrases.notes: Proof from local language that 'ויבן' can mean braiding.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 30 on behalf of the face view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the word, supported by local language
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'ויבן' must mean forming a body, which suits only the tail view.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'ויבן' means braiding her hair, which fits the face view.

steps.title: Another reading: חוה was built like a structure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives another explanation of 'ויבן'. רב חסדא (or a ברייתא) teaches that הקדוש ברוך הוא built חוה like a building. The description continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: 'And the Lord God built.' רב חסדא said, and some say it was taught in a ברייתא: This teaches that הקדוש ברוך הוא built חוה like the structure...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second way to read 'ויבן'. Here the word describes the shape of חוה's body, compared to a building. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This reading also lets the face view give meaning to 'built'. Instead of braiding, 'built' describes the shape הקדוש ברוך הוא gave her, modeled on a type of building. The exact comparison (what kind of building and why) comes in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא (a teaching of the תנאים outside the משנה)

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is cut off at 'like the structure'. The next passage finishes the comparison, so do not try to complete it from this passage alone.

phrases.english: Another explanation: 'And the Lord God built,'
Rav Chisda said,
and some say it was taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁבְּנָאָהּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְחַוָּה
phrases.english: this teaches that the Holy One, Blessed be He, built Eve
like the structure
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, different explanation of 'ויבן' alongside רבי שמעון בן מנסיא's braiding explanation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative interpretation of the same word
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'ויבן' has no clear meaning for the face view.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'ויבן' describes the building-like shape הקדוש ברוך הוא gave חוה (details continue on the next amud).
